content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published the second edition of its consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis (TB) prevention, specifically focusing on TB preventive treatment. This document, titled WHO Consolidated Guidelines on Tuberculosis: Module 1 – Prevention, is available in both electronic and print formats, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-009619-6 and 978-92-4-009620-2. The publication is copyrighted by WHO in 2024, with certain rights reserved under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO license. The guidelines were developed through collaboration among experts in public health policy, TB program management, and clinical care for TB patients. Successive Guideline Development Groups (GDGs) convened by WHO contributed to the recommendations, with the most recent meeting held in December 2023. The production and writing of the guidelines were coordinated by Avinash Kanchar, Dennis Falzon, Saskia den Boon, and Matteo Zignol, under the overall direction of Tereza Kasaeva, Director of the WHO Global Tuberculosis Programme. The GDG included professionals from various countries and specialties, such as Ménonli Adjibimey (Benin), Rolando Cedillos (El Salvador), Ana Ciobanu (Republic of Moldova), Alexander Kay (Eswatini), Naira Khachatryan (Armenia), Amir Khan (Pakistan), Blessina Kumar (India), Natalia Litvinenko (Ukraine), Mahshid Nasehi (Iran), Charisse Malbacias (Philippines), Alberto Matteelli (Italy), Norbert Ndjeka (South Africa), Senia Rosales Klintz (Sweden), Nicole Salazar Austin (USA), Susan Swindells (USA), Stavia Turyahabwe (Uganda), and Paran Winarni (Indonesia). The GDG was chaired by Norbert Ndjeka, with Lawrence Mbuagbaw (Canada) serving as the GRADE methodologist. External reviewers also contributed to the guidelines, including Helen Ayles (United Kingdom), Anurag Bhargava (India), Gavin Churchyard (South Africa), Raquel Duarte (Portugal), Amita Gupta (USA), Anthony D. Harries (France), Nino Lomtadze (Georgia), Ruslan Malyuta (UNICEF), Giovanni B. Migliori (Italy), Lindiwe Mvusi (South Africa), Anastasia Samoilova (Russia), Alena Skrahina (Belarus), Carrie Tudor (USA), and Valentina Vilc (Republic of Moldova). These reviewers provided critical feedback and ensured the guidelines' accuracy and comprehensiveness. The guidelines were funded by grants from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and Unitaid. WHO acknowledges the contributions of the Guideline Review Committee in reviewing and approving the guidelines prior to publication. The document also includes detailed annexes covering recommendations from the 2020 and 2024 editions, methods and expert panels, GRADE evidence summaries, and evidence-to-decision tables. Additionally, it features a survey exploring the feasibility of using levofloxacin for TB preventive treatment in contacts of multidrug-resistant TB cases.
